title: A2 Writing Quiz 10 — Nature, Environment & Local Places

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Have you ever planted a tree?
Have you ever plant a tree?
Did you ever planted a tree?
Have you ever plants a tree?
questions.explanation: Present perfect question: Have + subject + past participle: 'Have you ever planted a tree?'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We have visited that national park last spring.
We visited that national park last spring.
We have visit that national park last spring.
We are visiting that national park last spring.
questions.explanation: A finished time expression ('last spring') needs past simple, not present perfect.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We were walking along the river when we saw a deer.
We walked along the river when we were seeing a deer.
We were walk along the river when we saw a deer.
We walking were along the river when we saw a deer.
questions.explanation: Past continuous (background) + past simple (main event): 'We were walking... when we saw a deer.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This forest is greener than the one near my house.
This forest is more green than the one near my house.
This forest is greenest than the one near my house.
This forest is green than the one near my house.
questions.explanation: One-syllable adjectives take -er for comparatives: 'greener than'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This is the cleanest lake I've ever seen.
This is the more clean lake I've ever seen.
This is the most cleanest lake I've ever seen.
This is clean lake I've ever seen.
questions.explanation: One-syllable adjective superlative: 'the cleanest'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We should recycle more to protect the environment.
We should to recycle more to protect the environment.
We should recycling more to protect the environment.
We should recycles more to protect the environment.
questions.explanation: 'Should' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'should recycle'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Visitors must not feed the animals in the park.
Visitors must not feeding the animals in the park.
Visitors must not to feed the animals in the park.
Visitors must not fed the animals in the park.
questions.explanation: 'Must not' + base verb expresses a strict prohibition: 'must not feed'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We should have brought a map for the trail.
We should brought a map for the trail.
We should have bring a map for the trail.
We should has brought a map for the trail.
questions.explanation: 'Should have' + past participle expresses regret about the past: 'should have brought'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We're going to clean up the beach this weekend.
We're going clean up the beach this weekend.
We going to clean up the beach this weekend.
We're going to cleaning up the beach this weekend.
questions.explanation: 'Going to' + base verb expresses a plan: 'going to clean up'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If we protect the forest, animals will have a safe home.
If we will protect the forest, animals have a safe home.
If we protect the forest, animals have will a safe home.
If we protected the forest, animals will have a safe home.
questions.explanation: First conditional: If + present simple, will + base verb: 'If we protect..., animals will have...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I love exploring quiet forest trails.
I love to exploring quiet forest trails.
I love explore quiet forest trails.
I love explored quiet forest trails.
questions.explanation: 'Love' can be followed by a gerund (-ing form): 'love exploring'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The village decided protecting the old oak tree.
The village decided to protect the old oak tree.
The village decided protect the old oak tree.
The village decided for protect the old oak tree.
questions.explanation: 'Decide' is followed by the infinitive with 'to': 'decided to protect'.

questions.question: There isn't ___ pollution in this small village.
options: many
much
a few
several
questions.explanation: 'Pollution' is uncountable, so use 'much' in negative sentences.

questions.question: There are ___ birds singing in the trees this morning.
options: a little
a few
much
little
questions.explanation: 'Birds' is countable, and 'a few' means 'a small number of'.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses 'in order to'.
options: We planted trees in order to reduce pollution.
We planted trees in order reduce pollution.
In order to we planted trees reduce pollution.
We planted trees in order to reducing pollution.
questions.explanation: 'In order to' + base verb expresses purpose: 'in order to reduce pollution.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The lake will get worse unless we act now.
The lake will get worse unless we will act now.
The lake will get worse unless don't we act now.
The lake will get worse unless we acted now.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if not' and is followed by present simple: 'unless we act now.'

questions.question: There are many old trees ___ this river.
options: along
across
between
beyond
questions.explanation: 'Along' + noun describes something following the length of a place: 'along this river.'

questions.question: The small island is ___ the lake.
options: in the middle of
in middle of
on the middle
at the middle of
questions.explanation: 'In the middle of' + noun describes a central position: 'in the middle of the lake.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "I love hiking in the mountains.")
options: He said that he loves hiking in the mountains.
He said that he loved hiking in the mountains.
He said that he is loving hiking in the mountains.
He said he love hiking in the mountains.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, present simple usually shifts to past simple: 'he loved hiking in the mountains.'

questions.question: Which is the correct way to start an email to a local council about a park cleanup?
options: Hey guys,
Dear Sir/Madam,
Yo,
Hiya,
questions.explanation: 'Dear Sir/Madam,' is used when writing formally to an organization without knowing the recipient's name.

questions.question: Which is the correct way to end a formal email proposing a community cleanup?
options: Yours faithfully,
Catch you later,
Cheers,
Take care,
questions.explanation: 'Yours faithfully,' matches 'Dear Sir/Madam,' when the recipient's name is unknown.

questions.question: Choose the correct suggestion.
options: Why don't we organize a tree-planting day?
Why we don't organize a tree-planting day?
Why not we organize a tree-planting day?
Why don't we organizing a tree-planting day?
questions.explanation: 'Why don't we' + base verb is used to make a suggestion: 'Why don't we organize...'

questions.question: Which sentence correctly combines 'This is the trail.' and 'We saw wild deer there.'?
options: This is the trail who we saw wild deer.
This is the trail where we saw wild deer.
This is the trail which we saw wild deer.
This is the trail what we saw wild deer.
questions.explanation: 'Where' is used for places in relative clauses: 'the trail where we saw wild deer.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We often walk in the nearby forest at weekends.
We walk often in the nearby forest at weekends.
Often we walk in the nearby forest at weekends always.
We walk in the nearby forest often at weekends.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of frequency usually go before the main verb: 'We often walk in the nearby forest.'

questions.question: Which sentence has correct punctuation?
options: Do you know where the nearest recycling bin is?
Do you know where is the nearest recycling bin?
Do you know where the nearest recycling bin is.
Do you know, where the nearest recycling bin is?
questions.explanation: Indirect questions keep normal word order and end with a question mark: 'where the nearest recycling bin is?'

questions.question: We ___ litter from the park all morning, so it looks much cleaner now.
options: collect
have collected
have been collecting
collected
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous emphasizes an ongoing action explaining a present result: 'have been collecting'.

questions.question: This water bottle isn't mine, it's ___.
options: they
their
theirs
their's
questions.explanation: Possessive pronoun (stands alone, no noun after it): 'it's theirs.'

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses sequencing words.
options: First, collect the rubbish. Next, sort the recycling. Finally, plant new trees.
First collect rubbish next sort recycling finally plant trees.
Finally collect rubbish, first sort recycling, next plant trees.
Next first collect rubbish, finally sort plant trees.
questions.explanation: Sequencing words 'First,', 'Next,' and 'Finally,' organize steps clearly with commas.

questions.question: Every volunteer at the cleanup ___ a pair of gloves.
options: receive
receives
receiving
are receiving
questions.explanation: 'Every' takes a singular verb: 'Every volunteer receives...'

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: You haven't seen this trail before, have you?
You haven't seen this trail before, haven't you?
You haven't seen this trail before, did you?
You haven't seen this trail before, have?
questions.explanation: Negative statement + positive tag: 'You haven't seen this trail before, have you?'
